Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the MediCore Devices Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO; Sarah Jenkins, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Mike Thompson, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. MediCore Devices achieved record results this quarter, reflecting the strength of our diversified portfolio and our commitment to innovation.

Today, I will cover eight key aspects of our performance: capital equipment versus consumables mix trends; key assumptions underlying the guidance; R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress; SG&A expense management and efficiency gains; new product launches and contribution to growth; impact of pricing and cost management initiatives; organic revenue growth by segment and geography; and strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter.

Sarah will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Raj will update us on our technology advancements, and Mike will discuss our market strategies. We'll then conclude with a Q&A session.

Now, let's get started with capital equipment versus consumables mix trends.

As we dive into our Q2 results, our capital equipment versus consumables revenue mix continues to drive our predictable, high-margin revenue profile. Our business model follows the classic razor-razorblade dynamic in medtech—capital equipment includes upfront platform sales like our proprietary CardioFlow robotic-assisted PCI systems and next-gen imaging cath labs, while consumables are the high-recurring disposables such as guidewires, balloon catheters, drug-eluting stents, and our single-use FlexiGuide sheaths that generate annuity-like streams tied to procedure volumes.

In Q2, total revenue reached $1.28 billion, up 12% year-over-year on a reported basis and 14% at constant currency. Consumables accounted for 72% of total revenue, up from 68% in Q2 2023 and marking the sixth straight quarter of sequential expansion. That's $922 million in consumables sales, growing 18% year-over-year—well ahead of capital equipment, which was 28% of the mix at $358 million, up a more modest 4%. On a trailing twelve-month basis, consumables now make up 71% of total revenue, compared to 65% two years ago, showing the structural shift as our installed base matures.

Procedure growth is the key driver. Global procedure volumes for our enabled therapies—primarily percutaneous coronary interventions, TAVR adjuncts, and peripheral vascular interventions—rose 16% year-over-year to 1.2 million cases. This included a 22% surge in robotic-assisted PCI utilization on our CardioFlow platforms, where each procedure consumes an average of 2.3 kits versus 1.8 on legacy systems. Average selling prices for our premium consumables stayed firm at $2,450 per procedure kit, supported by our VALUE initiative—Value-Added Long-term Utilization Enhancement—which bundles AI-driven procedure optimization software with our stents to justify a 5-7% premium over commoditized alternatives from competitors like Boston Scientific or Medtronic.

Capital equipment trends are more measured, as expected. Shipments of new CardioFlow systems grew just 2% year-over-year to 145 units amid constrained hospital capex budgets due to inflation and staffing shortages. However, our installed base expanded to 4,200 systems globally, up 11%, with utilization rates climbing to 78% from 72% a year ago—thanks to remote software updates that boost procedure throughput without hardware changes. This is accelerating consumables pull-through, with a 92% system-level attachment rate, nearing the 95% we see at Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci base.

Regionally, the divergence stands out. In the U.S., 55% of Q2 revenue, consumables hit 76% of the mix—up 500 basis points year-over-year—due to strong Medicare reimbursement for robotic PCI under recent CMS APC updates and 25% procedure growth in ambulatory surgery centers. In EMEA, 22% of revenue, consumables were 68%; capital sales dipped 3% from DGUV reimbursement issues in Germany and UK NHS tender delays, but consumables grew 12% on PCI volumes in France and Italy. APAC, 18% of revenue and our fastest-growing region, had consumables at 70%, driven by 30% installed base expansion in China through our Mindray partnership for localized CardioFlow manufacturing, though capital softened in Japan from NHI pricing revisions.

We're leaning into this shift strategically. Our R&D team validated the next-gen CardioFlow 3.0 with haptic feedback and 4K imaging, piloting with 20 sites in Q3; early data indicates a 15% lift in procedure speed and consumables per case. We're scaling CircuLease, our flexible capital financing modeled after Stryker's approach, which bundled 35% of Q2 capital placements to smooth cycles and secure multi-year consumables commitments. Our $450 million VascuTech acquisition adds bioresorbable scaffolds that could boost consumables margins by 300 basis points through FY2025 via automated manufacturing.

Looking ahead, we expect consumables mix to hit 74-75% by year-end, with full-year consumables growth of 17-19% versus 5-7% for capital. While group purchasing organizations like Vizient pose ASP risks, our 65% gross margins on consumables—versus 45% on capital—offer cushion. This evolution de-risks our P&L and sets us up for mid-teens EPS growth, unlike peers stuck at 60/40 splits.

Now, let's talk about key assumptions underlying the guidance.

Turning to our FY24 guidance, we call for revenue growth of 9% to 11% at constant exchange rates, or $4.85 billion to $4.95 billion, with adjusted diluted EPS of $5.45 to $5.65. These targets blend organic growth, procedural tailwinds, and execution across Cardiovascular, Orthopedics, and Neuromodulation & Diabetes.

On organic revenue, we're assuming 8% to 10% constant-currency growth, outpacing the broader MedTech market's 5.5% to 6.5% per IQVIA. This anchors on 5% to 7% procedure volume expansion from pent-up elective demand and stabilizing hospital censuses. In Cardiovascular Interventions—45% of revenue—we model 6% to 8% U.S. TAVR growth, aligning with Edwards Lifesciences' data and our EvoCore valve ramp capturing 15% share in high-risk patients via the Evolut PRO+ delivery system. Globally, structural heart grows 7%, but we factor a 2-point FX headwind from a stronger USD.

Orthopedics, 30% of mix, assumes 4% to 6% procedure growth, with U.S. hip and knee volumes at 95% of pre-pandemic peaks per AAOS. Momentum from OmniFit porous titanium drives 12% U.S. growth post-510(k) expansions for robotic implantation and Stryker Mako partnerships. Pricing holds at +1% to +2% ASP uplift from value-based contracts, offsetting CMS CJR bundle compression. EMEA, 25% of segment sales, softens to 3% growth due to MDR delays like J&J's DePuy issues, but CE Mark renewals for cementless stems set up share gains.

Neuromodulation & Diabetes, 25% of revenue, eyes 10% to 12% organic growth. Diabetes assumes 8% CGM and pump adoption, tracking Dexcom G7 and our MiniMed 870G's 75% Time-in-Range gains. Neuromodulation leverages 15% U.S. SCS growth via Inceptiv2's AI burst algorithms outperforming Medtronic Intellis. APAC shines at 20% of segment with 12-14% China growth under NMPA fast-track for our Hugo RAS analogue, discounting NRDL volatility.

Geographically, U.S. mix rises to 58% on Medicare Advantage and capex recovery. EMEA at 22% assumes 4% growth amid German/French pricing, offset by UK NHS backlogs. APAC/China at 16% embeds 11% growth below Avalere's 15% forecast due to trade tensions on titanium. Rest of world steady at 4%.

P&L-wise, gross margins guide 66% to 67.5%, with 150 bps expansion from supply chain efficiencies—80% of FY24 resin and nitinol locked via contracts with Carpenter Technology, countering 3-4% inflation. OpEx flat at 48-49% of sales, R&D at 12.5% funding $450 million including NeuroBridge DBS Phase III and EvoNext robotic IDE. SG&A gains from digital sales cutting field costs 5% via VR simulations.

Macro assumes 5.2% healthcare spending growth per CMS, stress-tested for 1-point U.S. elective deferral. FX a 1.5% headwind. No major M&A baked in, but bolt-ons under $500 million opportunistic. We're gaining 100-150 bps share versus Boston Scientific in AFib and Abbott in CGM via Apple HealthKit interoperability.

This guidance builds on visible ramps, product cycles, and leverage—conservative for mid-teens EPS at midpoint and 15% ROIC.

Moving on to R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

Our R&D investment strategy and pipeline progress form a cornerstone of long-term value in medtech, driving revenue, margins, premium pricing, and share gains amid reimbursement and supply challenges.

First half R&D spend hit $1.28 billion, 12.4% of trailing twelve-month revenue of $10.3 billion—up 18% year-over-year, outpacing 9.2% organic growth and hitting our 3% above-industry target. Peers: Medtronic ~11%, Boston Scientific 13%, Intuitive 15%. Allocation: 45% core sustainment like TAVR and neuromod platforms, 35% robotics/AI breakthroughs, 20% digital therapeutics/bioresorbables.

This fuels our 10-year roadmap with 42 programs across Cardiovascular, Orthopaedics & Spine, Advanced Surgical Technologies, Neuroscience—on track for seven submissions, four launches by 2025, $4.2 billion peak sales, 40% of addressable opportunity.

Cardiovascular (45% allocation): $25B+ structural heart market at 12% CAGR. Lotus Edge TAVR, mirroring Edwards Sapien leadership, finished ORBIT III enrollment (1,200 patients, 45 sites)—95% success, 2.1% leak vs. 4-5% peers. FDA Q4, EU CE secured, Japan first-in-human with Terumo, China NMPA H1 2025 for 15% penetration in 35% growing market.

Orthopaedics & Spine (25%): $60B market with aging/post-COVID backlogs. Mako SmartRobotics (1.5M procedures) upgraded with AI planning, cutting OR time 22%. Trinity bioresorbable fusion Phase II: zero fractures in 150 implants vs. NuVasive. U.S. 14% growth, EMEA 8% share from DePuy.

Advanced Surgical (20%): $15B robotics/endoscopy. EndoAssist AI IDE-approved for 300-patient trial, 30% precision over laparoscopy. Wearable biosensor preclinical like Abbott Libre, human trials Q3 Europe. Reshored rare earths cut 10-15% inflation.

Neuroscience (10%): $12B neuromod/DBS. ReviStim DBS 85% IDE enrolled (500 patients), 42% tremor reduction vs. 28% peers like Medtronic Percept. China co-dev with MicroPort for 2026 $1.2B launch.

Optimizing via $450M YTD bolt-ons like digital health AI, NVIDIA partnerships, Mayo Clinic collab—timelines cut 12-18 months. 95% Phase III success vs. 70% industry. This powers 15-20% EPS CAGR, GAAP R&D at 11.5%.

Next, SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

Our SG&A management drove key margin expansion under our Path to Precision framework.

Q2 SG&A was $478 million, 27.8% of revenue—down 320 bps year-over-year, 150 bps sequentially, eighth straight quarter of leverage despite tough comps. $42 million below plan, $28 million EPS tailwind. Full-year now 28.0-28.5%, low end, $180 million savings vs. 2023.

Gains from digital transformation, standardization, sales optimization—for TAVR like Evoque, robotics like da Vinci.

Digital: AI revenue ops on Salesforce Einstein/MedDevice Analytics cut sales cycles 22% in U.S. EP via predictive scoring for pulsed-field labs. VR demos 65% interactions, 18% U.S. travel cut ($15M), 25% EMEA drop.

Standardization: Bangalore GSS (1,200 FTEs) digitized 95% payments, 45-to-18 day cycles, $22M discounts. G&A down 12%, 99.7% FDA compliance.

Sales: U.S. team flat at 2,800 reps, 112% attainment, $1.8M revenue/rep via hubs around Mayo. EM distributor shift cut APAC direct 8%, China SG&A -9% via local hubs.

U.S. (52% revenue) deleveraged 410 bps to 29.1%, Europe (28%) 520 bps to 25.4% post-pacemaker CE wins. Japan/APAC 15% growth, 3% spend.

Reinvesting 20% savings ($36M) in ICD remote AI for $500M SaaS by 2027 like CareLink. Targeting 100-200 bps annual leverage to mid-20s by 2026 amid inflation/tariffs/GLP-1.

This builds a high-margin engine for 12-15% EPS.

Then, new product launches and contribution to growth.

New launches drove 18% revenue growth, 32% of Q3 revenue (up from 22%), 42% organic on cohort.

Cardiology: VascuClear BioResorb FDA ramp, dissolves in 24 months vs. metallic issues. U.S. volumes +65% to 12,000, ASP $3,200, $145M (+110% YoY), edge in radial/bifurcation vs. Abbott Absorb.

Neuromod: NeuroPulse HFx EMEA June launch, AI adaptive for HF pain ($4.2B TAM, 12% CAGR), 40% opioid cut per INSPIRE. $78M, +28% seq, NICE/HTA wins.

Ortho: FlexiKnee AR, 22% time cut, 98% alignment, $112M, 15% U.S. ASC share vs. Stryker Mako.

Accretive: 250 bps gross margin to 68.5%, Galway scale, 15% COGS cut. $210M op income, 32% EBITDA vs. 25% legacy. R&D $320M (9% sales) on AI/bioresorb/robotics.

U.S. $1.2B (+25%), CMS OPPS +8%. Europe €220M (+35%), NHS 4,000 units vs. Medtronic. APAC +48%, China NMPA FlexiKnee, India Apollo.

Forward: 35-38% FY24 revenue, Q4 28-32% organic. $2.5B M&A like $450M NeuroDyne VNS. Q4 MediCloud AI beta, 30% readmit cut like Latitude. Sustainability: 70% metallic waste cut.

35-38% FY24, moat in scaffolds.

Then, impact of pricing and cost management initiatives.

Pricing/cost initiatives added $185M profitability, 320 bps gross to 68.2%, +15% EBITDA beat.

Pricing: 4.2% organic ASP, 3-5% FY target. Premiums: EvoFlow TAVR 12% over legacy (28% share, SEAL trial). Mix: 15% U.S. cardio to $2,450 PrecisionGuide (+180 bps).

U.S.: Offset CMS 2.7% NTAP cut via Kaiser VBC 5-7% escalators (2.5 pt readmit edge). Europe: 2.1% ASP, 8% UK/Nordics Vantage IPG. China flat ASP, +35% vol NRDL.

Costs: $112M savings (+20% target). Hedging 85% platinum/resins ($28M), dual nitinol 70% SE Asia (-11%). Galway/Plymouth automation 14% conversion cut, 92-97.5% yields ($45M). R&D realloc $22M, headcount -450 ($17M).

Net: Pricing 2.8 pts revenue, costs margins. AI pricing analytics +19% GPO wins. $150M digital AR neuromod. APAC 25% CAGR balance.

67-69% gross 2025.

Then, organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

Organic revenue grew 8.7%, accelerating from Q1 7.2%, beating midpoint—procedure volumes, share in structural heart/neuro, launches, reimbursement.

Cardiovascular (38%): 11.2%, TAVR Evolut FX+ +18% U.S. vs. Sapien, PulseSelect PFA +25%, coronary/PAD +9% Elute PRO 4% ASP. Galway efficiencies +120 bps to 72%.

Neuroscience (29%): 9.4%, DBS +14% Percept PC sensing vs. Vercise, SCS +8% Intellis adaptive +6% refills. Capital flat, consumables +11%. NeuroPace RNS for $2.5B epilepsy.

MedSurg/Diabetes (22%): 7.1%, endoscopy +12% GI Genius 1,200 sites +30% polyps, hernia +6%, diabetes +5% MiniMed 780G 250k units Simplera no-fingerstick vs. GLP-1, InPen bundle 20% T2 share.

Patient Monitoring/Respiratory (11%): 5.8%, ventilators +4%, 980 HNC APAC, Nellcor +7%.

U.S. (65%): 10.2%, OPPS +3.2% TAVR/NTAP Hugo +$15k/case, 105% pre-COVID.

EMEA (20%): 6.8%, NHS SynchroMed +15%, French HPPR endoscopy, +2% ASP.

APAC (10%): 12.5%, China +18% Evolut/MiniMed vs. Ultimaster, India endoscopy x2, Japan DBS +22%.

EM/Other (5%): 9.2%, Brazil/Mexico rebound.

$2.6B R&D Vertos/Kepler vs. da Vinci. FY24 8-9%, Q3 8.5-9.5%, 95% onshored.

Finally, strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter.

For Q4, after 9% organic (12% structural heart), priorities: innovation, go-to-market, resilience for mid-teens EPS FY25.

Innovation: EvoGuard TAVR U.S. ramp, 15% efficiency (45 min cases), AI nitinol, 25% share $150M inc. CE Japan 18% CAGR. NeuroPulse 2.0 Phase III, 30% battery vs. Proclaim XR, +$45M R&D FDA Dec, +8-10% pain $800M run-rate.

Expansion: APAC 12% IQVIA, 20 China specialists VizIR IVUS NRDL 30% $120M. EMEA 10% Helios sustainable PEEK EU MDR. EM $20M Brazil/SE Asia FreoFlex CGM 92% MARD 550M diabetes.

Excellence: Multi-source RF caths 60% Shield, 150 bps gross to 68% offset 3% FX. AI sales +5% prod $30M, 450 bps leverage. 25% plastics cut endoscopy GRI ESG.

Q4 10-12% organic, structural/neuro tailwinds, U.S. elective -2%, $4.25-4.45 EPS. $600B medtech 5.5% CAGR, 15% ROIC, bolt-ons digital.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah for a review of our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we delivered exceptional financial performance this quarter. Q2 revenue of $1.28 billion grew 12% reported, 14% constant currency, with consumables leading at 18%. Gross margins expanded 320 bps to 68.2% from pricing, mix, efficiencies. Adjusted operating margin hit 28.5%, up 250 bps, driving EPS of $1.42, +22% year-over-year. Full-year guidance reaffirmed: revenue $4.85-4.95B, EPS $5.45-5.65, with Q3 organic 8.5-9.5%. Cash flow strong at $650 million YTD, supporting $450 million bolt-ons and $1.2 billion share repurchase.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. We are excited about progress in our technology roadmap. Our latest innovation, CardioFlow 3.0, is poised to transform robotic-assisted PCI with haptic feedback and 4K imaging. We expect FDA approval in Q4.

Pipeline highlights include Lotus Edge TAVR FDA filing Q4, EndoAssist AI IDE trial, ReviStim DBS interim data, and Mako upgrades. R&D at 12.4% of sales funds 42 programs, seven submissions by 2025. We've derisked supply with reshoring and partnerships like NVIDIA, accelerating timelines.

Next, Mike with insights on our commercial strategy.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Raj. We are focused on commercial excellence and global reach. Strategic partnerships like Mindray in China and NHS tenders enable new markets. U.S. ASC growth +25%, EMEA CE wins, APAC +48% localized manufacturing. Sales force optimization via AI/VR boosts productivity 112%. Value-based contracts with Kaiser/IDNs secure escalators. Q4 priorities: EvoGuard ramp, VizIR China, sustainable lines for ESG.

Now, back to Elena for Q&A.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Thanks. Elena, on the consumables mix shift to 72%, how sustainable is the 92% attachment rate, and any risks from hospital capex constraints?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, David. The 92% attachment is durable, driven by CardioFlow utilization at 78% via software updates. Capex constraints slow new placements, but CircuLease bundled 35%, locking consumables. With installed base +11% to 4,200, procedure growth +16% pulls through. We're guiding 74-75% mix year-end, cushioned by 65% consumables margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Sarah, can you expand on SG&A leverage assumptions in guidance, especially with R&D up 18%?

Sarah Jenkins:
Absolutely, Lisa. SG&A deleveraged 320 bps this quarter to 27.8% via digital—VR 65% demos cut travel 18%, Bangalore GSS $22M discounts, sales prod +14% to $1.8M/rep. FY guide 28-28.5% embeds 100-200 bps annual leverage, offsetting R&D intensity. Reinvesting 20% in AI remote monitoring for SaaS upside.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Rivera with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mark Rivera:
Mike, on new launches like VascuClear, what's the Q4 contribution and competitive moat?

Mike Thompson:
VascuClear's bioresorbable edge—dissolves 24 months, radial/bifurcation—drove $145M Q3, +110%. Q4 we see 35-38% new cohort to revenue, U.S. CMS +8%, Europe +35%. Moat in magnesium alloy, 110% growth vs. Abbott, partnerships accelerating APAC.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Gupta with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Priya Gupta:
Raj, pipeline risks like AI regulatory scrutiny or China IP?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Valid point, Priya. FDA AI guidance addressed via 95% Phase III success—Lotus Edge 2.1% leak best-in-class. China mitigated by MicroPort co-dev, localized manufacturing. Reshoring rare earths cuts inflation. Timelines accelerated 12-18 months with NVIDIA/Mayo.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We remain confident in executing our strategy and delivering sustainable growth.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
